days.reason: This is the central account of Christ's Transfiguration. The text describes Jesus being transformed, the meeting with Moses and Elijah, and God's voice from the cloud confirming Jesus' divinity. This is the main scripture for this feast.

Here Jesus explains the connection between Elijah and John the Baptist, which is an important theological part of the Transfiguration event and the preparation for suffering. This links directly to the prophecy that Elijah must come before the Messiah.

The healing of the boy with seizures illustrates the contrast between the disciples' weak faith (which could not cast out the demon) and the divine glory they saw on the mountain. It emphasizes the need for prayer and fasting (v. 21) and the faith required to face the suffering predicted in v. 22-23.

Immediately after the Transfiguration, Jesus gives a new prediction of his suffering. This underscores the contrast between the glory of the mountain and the way to the cross, which is a central theme in the meaning of the Transfiguration (preparation for suffering).

The incident with the temple tax is the concluding part of the chapter and shows Jesus as Lord over the temple and its taxes. It links back to the temple and Moses/Elijah on the mountain, completing the theological unity of Matthew 17.
